A ("Some contestants who are not feeling well seldom get sick") and C ("Some contestants who are rarely sick feel unwell") assert essentially the same existential claim, so they are derivable or non-derivable together. Therefore A cannot be the single option that fails.

Under the reading where the unwell athletes are in the meeting, A, C and D all follow. Only B fails, because "seldom get sick" does not say how many sick people took part.

Under the strict reading, the unwell athletes did not participate and nothing says they are strong. Then A, C and D all fail and B follows, so no unique answer exists.

On neither reading is A the unique non-derivable option.
